measures.what_it_does: Authorizes Public Hospital District No. 1, Okanogan and Douglas Counties, to issue up to $48 million of general obligation bonds, maturing within 30 years, to renovate, remodel and equip Three Rivers Hospital in Brewster (central entrance, ambulance bay, operating rooms, radiology, building systems), repaid by excess property taxes. Needs 60%.
measures.cost_line: Up to $48 million over up to 30 years; an estimated $0.73 per $1,000 of assessed value, about $18 a month on a $300,000 home.
measures.pro_summary: Michael Pruett, hospital board chair: vote yes to keep quality health care close to home, modernize a 77-year-old building and keep local care strong during wildfires and emergencies.
measures.con_summary: Melvin Sorensen (planokanoganhealth.net): don't commit $48 million and 30 years of taxes without a county-wide study; the county's three small hospitals compete, and if Three Rivers fails, residents keep the tax with no hospital.

taxes.basis: A yes vote adds a new 30-year excess property tax, an estimated $0.73 per $1,000; it is a new levy, not a renewal.

spending.basis: A yes vote funds a $48 million capital investment in the public hospital; the opposing argument is a study-first case for restraint.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA guide record 7283 (S1); Methow Valley News 2026-09-24 and 2025-11-13 (S2, S3); Methow Valley Examiner 2025-11-07 (S4).

measures.what_it_does: Continues Brewster's emergency medical services property tax levy, first approved in 2020, for six years from 2027; the city uses it to contract with Douglas-Okanogan Fire District 15 for ambulance and EMS service.
measures.cost_line: $0.50 or less per $1,000 of assessed value a year for 2027-2032, the same rate as the expiring levy.
measures.pro_summary: No statement for was filed; the levy keeps the city's EMS contract with Douglas-Okanogan Fire District 15 funded.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition committee was found.

taxes.basis: A yes vote renews an expiring EMS levy at the same maximum rate rather than raising it, so +1.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA guide record 7278 (S1); RCW 84.52.069 (S2); Omak-Okanogan County Chronicle 2020 and 2026 (S3, S4).

measures.what_it_does: One-year excess levy for Twisp's share of Aero Methow Rescue Service's plan to staff a second advanced-life-support ambulance year-round, on top of the town's regular EMS levy. Needs 60% and minimum turnout.
measures.cost_line: $0.10 per $1,000 of assessed value, collected in 2027 only; about $25,000 from Twisp.
measures.pro_summary: Aero Methow and the Town Council: calls rose from 531 in 2015 to 911 in 2025, the valley is over an hour from a hospital, and a seasonal second ambulance ran about $310,000 over cost in 2026.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition committee was found.

taxes.basis: A yes vote adds a new one-year property tax on top of the regular EMS levy.

spending.basis: A yes vote expands ambulance staffing from seasonal to year-round.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA guide record 7279 (S1); Methow Valley News 2026-07-23, 2026-07-09, 2026-02-19 and 2026-08-06 (S2-S5).

measures.what_it_does: One-year excess levy for Winthrop's share of Aero Methow Rescue Service's plan to staff a second advanced-life-support ambulance year-round, on top of the town's regular EMS levy. Needs 60% and minimum turnout.
measures.cost_line: $0.10 per $1,000 of assessed value, collected in 2027 only; about $20,000 from Winthrop.
measures.pro_summary: Aero Methow, backed by the Town Council: rising calls make it a de facto urgent care center, and it feels 'obligated to prepare to respond' to demand.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition committee was found.

taxes.basis: A yes vote adds a new one-year property tax on top of the regular EMS levy.

spending.basis: A yes vote expands ambulance staffing from seasonal to year-round.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA guide record 7280 (S1); Methow Valley News 2026-07-09, 2026-07-23, 2026-02-19 and 2026-08-06 (S2-S5).

measures.what_it_does: One-year excess levy across the rural Methow Valley EMS District (outside Twisp and Winthrop) so Aero Methow Rescue Service can hire three paramedics and staff a second advanced-life-support ambulance year-round. Needs 60% and minimum turnout.
measures.cost_line: $0.10 per $1,000 of assessed value, collected in 2027 only; about $47 on a $500,000 house, per Aero Methow.
measures.pro_summary: Aero Methow: calls nearly doubled in ten years, the regular levy is at its 50-cent maximum and covers about 60% of operations; county commissioners placed it on the ballot unanimously.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition committee was found.

taxes.basis: A yes vote adds a new one-year property tax on top of a regular EMS levy already at its legal maximum.

spending.basis: A yes vote expands service from a seasonal to a year-round second ambulance.

measures.what_it_does: Resets the Oroville-area fire district's regular property tax levy to $0.50 per $1,000 for 2027 collection (Resolution No. 97), for fire protection, life safety, apparatus and equipment, and firefighter safety; the 2027 amount becomes the base for later limits.
measures.cost_line: From about $0.22 to $0.50 per $1,000 of assessed value for 2027 collection.
measures.pro_summary: Denise Dhane: Oroville relies on volunteer firefighters who respond within minutes; a severe fire season and rising fuel, equipment and training costs strain the budget.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition committee was found.

taxes.basis: A yes vote more than doubles the district's regular levy rate, from about $0.22 to $0.50 per $1,000, and resets its base.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA guide record 7281 (S1); RCW 84.55.050 (S2). No press coverage found.
